Full layouts of pipe inode info, pipe buffer, pipe operations, preallocation pool, file, inode and dentry structures beyond observed fields.
Implementations of pipe lock and unlock, pipe empty and occupancy helpers, buffer lookup, readability and watch queue presence checks.
Implementations of pipe file creation, buffer confirmation, page copy to and from iterators, time updates and descriptor management.

findings.text: Boot time setup for process identity pseudo filesystem initializes its inode hash table, creates a slab cache for attribute objects with alignment and accounting and fail fast behavior, mounts the internal instance and publishes the global mount and root path, aborting boot on hash, cache or mount failure.
Minimum default pipe buffer count is two.
Default maximum pipe size starts at 1048576 bytes and per user page accounting starts with no hard allowance and a soft allowance scaled from PIPE_DEF_BUFFERS and INR_OPEN_CUR.
Acquiring two pipes together requires distinct pipes and a stable address order for both acquisitions to avoid deadlock, with a helper comparator that orders synchronization maps by address.
Anonymous pipe page pool behaves as a bounded last in first out stack limited by PIPE_PREALLOC_MAX that reports empty on underflow and rejects overflow without modification.

Write path sizes page need from total request length capped by PIPE_PREALLOC_MAX, samples current pool fill without locking, allocates shortfall outside the lock, then under the lock retains only what fits and frees the rest, while completion path drains the pool down to PIPE_PREALLOC_KEEP under the lock and frees surplus after unlock.

Anonymous pipe page acquisition prefers pooled pages before allocating new pages with GFP_HIGHUSER and __GFP_ACCOUNT with the pipe mutex held, return of a page recycles it only when exclusively owned and pool space exists and otherwise frees it, release delegates to that return path, and steal succeeds only for exclusively owned pages where it drops memory accounting and marks the page locked.

Generic pipe buffer helpers manage page lifetime by reference count where acquisition succeeds only when a reference can be taken, release drops a reference, and steal succeeds only when the pipe holds the sole reference and then locks the page.
Anonymous pipe buffer operations table binds release and steal to anonymous pipe variants and acquisition to the generic helper.

Consuming a ring slot releases its buffer then advances the tail index, using the read wait spinlock with interrupt exclusion plus PIPE_BUF_FLAG_LOSS handling when a watch queue is present and a plain mutex protected update otherwise.

Anonymous pipe read reports zero for empty requests, otherwise consumes available ring data up to the requested extent while holding the pipe mutex, emits a meta loss notification first when flagged using ENOBUFS for too small extent and EFAULT for copy failure, respects PIPE_BUF_FLAG_PACKET boundaries and PIPE_BUF_FLAG_WHOLE atomicity with ENOBUFS when caller extent is too small, confirms buffers before copying with confirmation or EFAULT errors propagated, sleeps interruptibly with exclusive wakeup when empty yet writers remain unless O_NONBLOCK or IOCB_NOWAIT selects EAGAIN failure, stops at writer absence or after partial progress with ERESTARTSYS on interruption when nothing was read, trims the page pool on exit and wakes writers on transition from full plus readers and async writers as needed.
Ring fullness is determined by comparing occupancy derived from head and tail against a limit, with a convenience check that applies the pipe current maximum.
First in first out read delegates to anonymous pipe read and records access time on positive transfer, where access time update is skipped when O_NOATIME is set.

Packet mode is selected by O_DIRECT on the file, and writability holds when occupancy is below the current maximum or when no readers remain, evaluated from a consistent snapshot of indices and limit.

Anonymous pipe write rejects watch queue pipes with EXDEV, reports zero for empty requests, fails with EPIPE and optional SIGPIPE unless IOCB_NOSIGNAL suppresses the signal when no readers exist, otherwise merges a partial page tail into a last buffer checked via PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE when possible and appends new pages marked with PIPE_BUF_FLAG_PACKET or PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE with EFAULT on copy failure and ENOMEM on allocation failure, blocks interruptibly for space unless O_NONBLOCK or IOCB_NOWAIT selects EAGAIN failure or a pending signal selects ERESTARTSYS, drops the lock while waiting and reevaluates emptiness after wakeup, trims the page pool on exit and wakes readers on transition from empty or edgetrigger mode plus writers and async readers as needed.
First in first out write delegates to anonymous pipe write and on positive transfer attempts a filesystem write guard to refresh modification time, propagating time update failure as the result.

Pipe control supports FIONREAD querying total buffered bytes by summing buffer lengths under the lock and copying the result to user space, plus IOC_WATCH_QUEUE_SET_SIZE and IOC_WATCH_QUEUE_SET_FILTER delegated when that feature is enabled, rejecting other commands with ENOIOCTLCMD.

Poll registers read and write wait entries before sampling state for files opened with FMODE_READ and FMODE_WRITE, latches a pseudo edge trigger flag on first EPOLLET read poll, reports EPOLLIN and EPOLLRDNORM when the ring is non empty and EPOLLHUP when writers are gone with an unmatched write generation, and reports EPOLLOUT and EPOLLWRNORM when not full plus EPOLLERR when readers are gone.

Release adjusts reader and writer counts under the lock according to FMODE_READ and FMODE_WRITE, when exactly one direction disappears wakes all readers and writers and emits SIGIO with POLL_IN and POLL_OUT async signals in both directions, then drops the pipe reference and reports success.
Asynchronous notification setup applies separately to read and write directions under the lock and undoes the read registration if the write registration fails.

Global pipe mount pointer is immutable after early initialization, pipe dentries are named from their inode number in a pipe bracket style through a dedicated name helper bound in dentry operations, with anonymous pipe file operations forward declared.

Internal pipe creation validates flags against O_CLOEXEC plus O_NONBLOCK plus O_DIRECT plus O_NOTIFICATION_PIPE with EINVAL on disallowed bits, creates the file pair, allocates read and write descriptors, audits the pair and returns descriptors, unwinding files and descriptors on failure, while the kernel variant installs both files on success.

User facing pipe creation copies the descriptor pair to user memory and unwinds files and descriptors with EFAULT on copy failure, with a two argument form passing caller flags and a one argument form passing no flags.
Waiting for writability must release the pipe lock before sleeping on the write wait until the writability predicate holds and then reacquire the lock.

Observed pipe state comprises ring head and tail indices with a maximum usage limit, reader and writer counts with a write generation counter, read and write wait queues, per direction async queues, a mutex, a page preallocation pool, a watch loss indicator and a pseudo edge trigger flag.

Blocking pipe input output must not sleep while holding the pipe mutex and must revalidate reader presence, emptiness or fullness and pending signals after wakeup to avoid lost wakeups and use after close.

Head is sampled with acquire ordering against concurrent notification posting and tail advancement with loss reporting is serialized by interrupt excluded spinlock when watchers exist, while occupancy and poll checks use single snapshots to avoid torn index reads.

Unlocked sampling of pool fill can race with concurrent refill and drain, so allocation is bounded and performed outside the lock with only fitting pages retained under the lock and all surplus freed outside the lock.
Pipe helpers for double locking, generic buffer acquisition release and steal, kernel pipe creation and writable waiting have external linkage for use outside this file.
